steps.text: The icy wind slowly comes to a stop.
An azure lake gleams above the vast, tranquil snowfield.
Kjerag's winters are cold, and the water freezes over naturally, yet its surface remains a mirror, softly reflecting the blue of the sky.
A figure appears at the center of the lake.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr? Is that you?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Enya...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr...?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: What should I call you... Kjarr, or Kjeragandr?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Oh you... Surely you haven't forgotten?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Kjeragandr is what the people of the past named me.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: But Kjarr? Kjarr shall always be head maid to the lady Enya.
Enya thought of many things she wanted to say during her long journey here.

These thoughts sway through her mind alongside all the questions she wants to ask, like a cup filled to the brim. From time to time it would make some noise, but now that she looks inside after her eternity of waiting, she finds it dry, long dry.
What should she say? What could she say?

spans.text: What should she say? What
could
she say?

steps.text: The friend she was searching for stands before her, her warm hands caressing her cheeks and the tip of her nose. Just like she always did.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: While I can't say it's entirely unexpected, I am still pleasantly surprised you managed to find this place in the end.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I was really worried about you, Kjarr...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I didn't know where you went, and the people were terrified after the Catastrophe struck. I had no choice but to go on the Pilgrimage as the Saintess.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I went by many places... before ultimately discovering these ruins atop Mount Karlan.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Did you say... you went on the Pilgrimage? In this season? You... You idiot!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Well...

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Ah, forgive me. As a maid, I should not speak to the Saintess in such a manner.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Enya... I'm just glad you're alright.
Her friend's voice is still as dear as it ever was.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Those visions I saw just now, were they the Kjerag of the past?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: They were. Those were my memories.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Memories of when I walked the land alongside the people countless years ago. The tale of how the Kjerag of then became the Kjerag of today.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: You are here in the forbidden land of Kjeragandr's body, and so through her eyes, you may witness history a thousand years past.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I'm... in Kjeragandr's body?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: How should I explain it... You started in my arm and crawled your way into my chest.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: This lake... Is it an illusion?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Is this the Heart of Karlan?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: The Heart of Karlan is actually the name of this lake. What you see is how it was a thousand years ago.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: At the time, in the depths of the mountains, there was a lake that remained unfrozen year-round.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Desperate wanderers discovered this precious source of water, and here they took root and multiplied. In time, they came to see it as a heart.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: 'The heart pulsed, and Karlan's flesh began to grow.'

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: And so the people built an altar here, so that they may honor the miracle that Kjeragandr blessed them with...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I saw the statue in the ruins. It was huge, exquisite.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Completely unlike the statue by Lake Silberneherze that we referenced ancient texts for. Was it something only people who have seen the real 'you' could have made?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: What... are you, Kjarr?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Hooh... Now that's a question and a half. What a headache...

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: A very, very, very long time ago, I only knew that my body was massive, no different from the mountains and rivers themselves.

spans.text: A very, very,
very
long time ago, I only knew that my body was massive, no different from the mountains and rivers themselves.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: The land once teemed with my kin. Before that darkness descended, they already had names assigned to them by beings of the past.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: 'Feranmuts', 'children of the planet', 'lords of the land'...

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: In comparison, I am not that much older than your most ancient civilizations.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: If you were to ask me, I prefer to see myself as a form of life. Really, I much prefer the name Kjeragandr.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Unfortunately, I am not what the people crave. I am not a 'god' who has power over all.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: But they still treat you as one. They believe in the commandments you have given, and ascribe everything to you, good and bad.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: And those Saintesses, they...

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: That was not my intention.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: I once went to sleep for a time, but apparently, my departure terrified the people. As they tried to search for me, to rouse me, they became lost.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: I sealed this place away, in the hope that the people would forget this terrible mistake of the long past.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I know that, of course I do!

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You're not some evil, sinister spirit who would smile in the face of innocent girls freezing to death...
Enya raises her hands, holding onto the warm hands cupping her cheeks.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: I am not the god the people need... nor have I ever given any commandments.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: I am nothing but another one of the lives born upon this land, born without rhyme or reason. How could I possibly have any wise words of survival to pass on?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: But when I took the form of man and walked among you, I discovered to my surprise that though your people are frail, you possess an innate, near-instinctual power.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: One that allows you to help one another, to overcome all difficulties and survive upon this dangerous land.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: In your language, this power is known as 'virtue'.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: So... that's how it all came to be...

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: It was not I who taught you, but rather, it was you who taught me the meaning of life.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: As for the name of Kjeragandr, and the form that represents Her, those are creations of men.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: But I do not believe them to be lies. The name of Kjeragandr is how the power you wield manifests itself. Nothing more.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: I think... this is the Kjeragandr you seek.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: 'And so She said: my path is, in the end, your path...'

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: People tried to confirm Her appearance, but ultimately, they were only attempting to see clearly who they themselves were.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: But the paths people walk are for the most part not level roads. Most of the time, they are like confused burdenbeasts, circling about the same place, over and over...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: The people of Kjerag once brought you back among us, and so our faith was steadied...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjarr... Will you come back?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Enya...

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: I think... I can't stay by your side, this time around.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...But you promised me.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You told me that you wouldn't just leave all of a sudden, that She wouldn't simply spirit you away...

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Enya... Listen to me, Enya.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: I'm afraid I have to break my promise this time... but I never meant to lie to you. Never.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: You are my friend. Out of countless years and countless people, my one and only friend.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: I wanted to accompany you forever, until the end of your days... I even thought I would be the one left behind, to endure our separation.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: But... what happened?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: What could possibly have happened to force you to leave?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: There is no such thing as an eternal union. Parting is simply a matter of time.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: And my time has come... That is all.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I just didn't want the day to come so quickly.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Things happen at their most suited hour.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: You are unlike the other children who call out my name. You are not some helpless girl waiting for my answer as you are pushed about.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...I started out the same as them.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: But now, you walk the path of your own choosing.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: You were able to find the solution in your own heart. You have braved great trials I know nothing of, experienced great danger I could not help you with. And now, you stand before me.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: You are my Enya. My sweet, sweet Enya.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: You are the little burdenbeast who managed to jump the fence. You have a heart that resists all discipline and a bright, witty mind. You are the first Saintess to come pray with resentment and bitterness in her heart.
The snows of Karlan are tall and far, as pure white as stacked clouds. The wind blows from deep ravines, gently sweeping by the great land of Kjerag.
Snowflakes fall from the wind's embrace and melt with spring. They travel through Karlan's streams into the lake, then seep into the depths of the earth.
From there, the sun's rays lift the water, the mists returning to the horizon. They pile up into clouds, before turning into the next round of snow.
Their hands refuse to let go of each other. The warmth as they lean upon one another lights a spark in their bodies.

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Go, Enya.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...But where?

steps.name: Kjeragandr
steps.text: Go drive away the last of the darkness, and usher in a new tomorrow.
The illusion disappears, like waking from a dream. The cave is still as gloomy as it was earlier. The Saintess of Kjerag turns to the massive statue.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...Drive away the last of the darkness, usher in... a new tomorrow.
Broken clumps of snow spiral around her, before being dispersed by the wind.
A single snowflake remains in the palm of her hand. A perfect, flawless hexagon.
It does not melt, nor flit through the air. It simply waits quietly like a guardian, unmoving for eons.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Not even asking me my opinion before giving this to me... You know I don't like taking the spotlight...

spans.text: Not even asking me my opinion before giving this to me... You
know
I don't like taking the spotlight...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: You're just so willful...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: AHHHH—!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Thank goodness, you're finally awake!

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Did I... pass out?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: You did! Both of you did when Enya touched the statue. You've been out for about five minutes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I didn't think it would be that short a time...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Did you... see it?

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: I did!

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: I had a terrible nightmare. I was chasing down some game, when my illness suddenly got a lot worse. My entire arm turned to stone...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: But then I saw someone who looked a lot like Kjeragandr, and she cured me in my dream.

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Then she comforted me, telling me the stone disease isn't Kjeragandr's punishment, and that I'm not a bad girl...

steps.name: Joanna
steps.text: Saintess! Could she have... been Kjeragandr Herself? We... We found Her, right?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: We did. That must have been Kjeragandr you saw.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: What are you two talking about? How come I'm the only one who didn't see anything?

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Don't worry about it.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: She simply gave each of us the answer we needed.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Enya... I...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Maybe... Maybe I need to revise my hypothesis and calculations.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: If it wasn't a special vein of ore that protected Kjerag from Catastrophe for a millennium... Add to that all we've seen in this cave...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Though I still can't bring myself to believe in things like Feranmuts, which are completely incompatible with our scientific system...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: But... having eliminated everything false, then the only possibility left must be the truth, no matter how absurd it may be.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Enya, could you tell me...?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: The Kjeragandr you saw... What was...?
The Saintess stretches out her hand, softly stroking the perplexed woman's head, treating her like any other devotee who has come to her for confession.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I can't explain what the Kjeragandr in our hearts is, in scientific terms...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: But as a scientist, how could you possibly fear the unknown?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I would never—

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Kjeragandr might not be something completely incompatible with science.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Perhaps you have discovered a little corner of a field that science has yet to set foot on?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: ...Oh, shoot.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: When we were climbing the mountain, the Catastrophe warning went up another level.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Basically, within the next three hours, there's a seventy-two percent chance Kjerag will be hit by a second Catastrophe.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Enya, we need to go and tell everyone to evacuate right away—

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: We won't make it in time...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...I still have one last thing I must do.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Wait, where are you going—
Elena and Joanna follow along behind Enya, the three of them running through the passage they came through.
At the entrance of the cave, they see a familiar figure once again.
They are unsure why, but in the short time they were away, the old man seems to have aged ten years.

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: I saw...

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: I saw Her, and Her footprints in the snow...

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: I was... an unforgivable, faithless man... all along...
The elder of the Vine-Bead Court falls to the ground, as if all the strength has been sapped from him.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: ...I once endured the tangling of love and pain alongside a friend, as we waited for daybreak to wash over the mountains.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: The road we walked was far longer than the road leading up Karlan.

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: You...
The Saintess's finger traces out a shallow arc across the old man's forehead, from left to right.
Her fingertip streaks across his graying brow, anointing him with unmelted snow, like how the most pious of Kjerag clerics would dispel spirits and make prayers for newborn babes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I still remember her. The girl who would ask me to teach her, even when it came to darning clothes.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: How the living should be saved, how order should operate... You did not know, but She... was also learning from you.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: She watches all you do. She wishes to walk with you, whether you walk down the right path or the wrong.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: She never meant to deny you.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Her Saintess has heard your confession, and in Her name, absolves you of your sin of disbelief.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: By Kjeragandr, you walk with Her.
Unstoppable tears flow from his aged eyes. They seep into the earth, like fallen snow.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I must admit, I once looked down upon you, and upon Kjerag.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: That battleship behind you is the result of over a decade of painstaking nation-building.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Although I am not entirely sure why you changed your mind on keeping your 'secret weapon' here concealed...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: But no matter. If one were to survey the entirety of Terra, how many people who could do all this would one find?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You have earned my praise, Silverash.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I thank Your Grace for your approval, but as I see it, what is more regretful is that...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If Victoria were still the mighty empire it once was, you would not pay much heed to the profit you could extract from a measly speck such as Kjerag.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Who would have thought the prediction that arrogant youth gave during that one banquet would become so dangerously accurate?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: In the end, there are none who can save Victoria from its misfortunate decline.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Though it is not hard to see where history's river is taking you, to change its course requires the hand of fate on your side. There is pride to be had in your foresight.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I have never been scornful of your talent. In all truth, I have had my fair share of wondering how things would be now had I kept you in Victoria back then.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Would you be a general with the name of Caster, or perhaps a famed marquis? A future where... I would not have curtailed whatever achievements you acquired.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Regardless of the details, it would have been much better than the situation we find ourselves in now.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: If this is what Your Grace truly believes, then I hope there is still the opportunity to accept such an invitation.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Oh, don't make that sort of joke, or I might just start expecting it.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I presume you have exhausted all the words of rancor in your heart to curse my dastardly cunning?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I never had any in the first place. If you lose the wager, you must pay. This is the most basic of preparations any player of this game would have made.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Besides, you are simply here to retrieve the profits you are owed from the many years of trade between Victoria and Kjerag.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But no matter. I must thank you for coming here in person today to sign this agreement with me. You will be giving Kjerag a priceless opportunity.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Haha... A priceless opportunity?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Let us return to the topic at hand. You being here must mean you agree to all contents of the pact.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: All contents? I am afraid not... I must dissent with the agreement's particulars.

spans.text: All
contents? I am afraid not... I must dissent with the agreement's particulars.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Oho, you still wish to bargain, even at this hour?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Alright then, let's hear it. Which clauses do you disagree with?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I know you intend for Caster and Kjerag to start a joint mining program, so that you may partake in forty percent of the extraction of Kjerag's minerals, including Originium and Oriron.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: By my reckoning, this number could be increased to eighty percent.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Kjerag has ample mineral wealth, enough for the development of both our nations.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Victoria will offer mining equipment and specialist training to Kjerag as a means of aid, and we are more than happy to welcome in the workers and technology consultants you send.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: However... we will, from now on, not allow a single Victorian soldier to pass our borders.

spans.text: However... we will, from now on, not allow a
single
Victorian soldier to pass our borders.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Ah, yes, the one clause regarding 'the distribution of mineral extraction profits between Victoria and Kjerag as dictated by equal negotiation'. I have my issues with that as well.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Kjerag shall have complete and absolute sovereignty over all resources within our borders. Victoria has no right to interfere.

spans.text: Kjerag shall have complete and absolute sovereignty over all resources within our borders. Victoria has
no
right to interfere.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: In regards to Victorian aid, we give our thanks. Victoria shall enjoy preferential prices for all commodities Kjerag sells her.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Naturally, the aid you have offered shall be repaid in equivalent value, so Victoria must import a sufficient amount of goods from Kjerag on an annual basis—the amount of which shall also be decided by Kjerag.

spans.text: Naturally, the aid you have offered shall be repaid in equivalent value, so Victoria
must
import a sufficient amount of goods from Kjerag on an annual basis—the amount of which shall also be decided by Kjerag.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Don't be like this, Enciodes.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Such unreasonable demands ill behoove one conceding defeat.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: 'Conceding defeat'? I do not recall ever uttering such words during my time aboard the Gloriana.

spans.text: 'Conceding defeat'? I do not recall ever uttering such words during my time aboard the
Gloriana.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Why exactly do you think I would agree to your revisions? You've lost your mind.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I have faith that you will agree.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: ...What in the...?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: This is the bargaining chip I have brought with me today.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I am terribly sorry. We are of the belief that using military force to dictate a bilateral agreement is hardly reasonable.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But this may be the only form of negotiation you are willing to accept.

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: What was that?!

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: Who's firing at us?!

steps.name: Victorian Officer
steps.text: It's that battleship! Dammit, there's only the one, how can it have that much firepower?!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: No, that's not it!

steps.name: Victorian Soldier
steps.text: It looked like the cannonfire came from the mountains!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Keep them coming!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Keep those hands moving, don't give the Victorians a chance to breathe!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: You there, big guy. Can't you load these shells any faster?

steps.name: Tschäggättä
steps.text: On it, ma'am!

steps.name: Yucatan
steps.text: You shouldn't be moving about so much, Rus. You need to mind your health—

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Shut it!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Enciodes stashed some lovely little things up here in the mountains, and I finally have a golden opportunity to play with these new toys!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: On my order! Aim at Caster's flagship, then fire!

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Let them get a taste of Kjeragandr's protection!

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Madam Sciurus, the mission Sir Enciodes entrusted us with was intimidating Caster's fleet. Please keep in mind that he is still aboard the Gloriana.

spans.text: Madam Sciurus, the mission Sir Enciodes entrusted us with was
intimidating
Caster's fleet. Please keep in mind that he is still aboard the
Gloriana.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: If you do not follow the plan, I shall be forced to stop you.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: I know, I know... Sheesh, can't even take a joke.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: These are the secrets my sister and Enciodes had been keeping quiet about this whole time.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: You really are something, Weiss. The Victorians were scouring the mountains for Enciodes's arsenal, but they never would've expected it was right in front of their eyes, in our logistics vehicles.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: I can't believe she'd hide this even from me... Ratatos, the next time I see you, I'm going to—

spans.text: I can't believe she'd hide this even from
me
... Ratatos, the next time I see you, I'm going to—

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: This was the most... crucial mission Sir Enciodes gave me.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: These weapons... Their scale, their very existence, is Kjerag's greatest secret. Even now.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: We still need to keep quiet about them. Our biggest trump card is that the Victorians have no idea how much military power we have.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: We need to keep Caster's judgment off-balance.

steps.name: Weiss
steps.text: Nobody can really say what would happen if her fleet really did take one step forward, after all...

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: I am well aware of the situation right now. You don't need to explain it to me bit by bit.

steps.name: Sciurus
steps.text: Ratatos... This time, make sure you take care of yourself...

steps.name: Trilby Asher
steps.text: (Whispers) Your Grace, we still have no way of confirming the artillery's whereabouts.

steps.name: Trilby Asher
steps.text: We have informed all ships to enter defense mode—

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: No need for your report. All you need to know is that, at this very moment, there are enough large-scale cannons in Mount Karlan to shred the entirety of your fleet.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: All your ships are within range.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: ...You think two shells is enough for me to believe you have the power to annihilate my fleet?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: D5, east, two hundred meters.
The moment Enciodes speaks, a precision shell lands by the eastern flank of the Gloriana. The blast wave lifts up the hems of the pair's clothes.

spans.text: The moment Enciodes speaks, a precision shell lands by the eastern flank of the
Gloriana
. The blast wave lifts up the hems of the pair's clothes.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It seems there is no need for further proof.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Surely this weaponry is not the product of your own research?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Which of them has been helping you, Gododdin? Normandy?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Is that really such an important question right now?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: You may cut off Kjerag's connections to our allies, but we have our ways of finding new ones.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Such painstaking effort just for your opening...

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Merely tactics we were forced to use.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: With such limited time, Kjerag's military development had no choice but to pursue another specialization.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Even if we were given another ten years, I fear Kjerag would still be unable to muster up a fleet that could stand against yours.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But it seems your formidable vessels have made you forget that the battlefield is not only a clash between warships.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Kjerag only means to defend ourselves, and we have no intention of robbing other nations of their coin. So compared to high-speed battleships, we went for a more suitable option.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Our mountains form a natural barrier. When lined with artillery, they serve as a natural shield, an aegis you have no hope of breaking.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But when all is said and done, if you had not prematurely treated these 'negotiations' as a surrender, you would not have fallen into such passivity.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Then... You are determined to open hostilities with me today.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Hardly, hardly.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Just as how your fleet did not come here with intent to wage war with Kjerag, my goal today is simply to facilitate a discussion.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I too have prepared an agreement for you. It contains various clauses on things such as tariffs between Victoria and Kjerag and our joint mining projects. You may look over it now.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Once you have signed it, Kjerag will be happy to escort you back safely to Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You think you can threaten me like this, child?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Too radical a stance at the negotiating table will only serve to betray your lack of confidence.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: If I call your bluff and order my ships forward, then things will get ugly.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It would be an incredible shame.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I had considered this possibility before I came to these talks.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: It's just that, if people far in the future were to discuss how the Duke of Caster and some insignificant nobody died fighting each other in the snow, why, that would certainly bring shame to the Caster name, perhaps even all Victoria.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: But in Kjerag? If I am gone, there are countless others who will do what I would have done. They will continue developing Kjerag until she has become a nation none can sneer at.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I know that accepting such an unfair agreement must also be a difficult choice for you.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I can give you half an hour—but know this. For every minute you hesitate, all energy prices mentioned in the agreement will increase, just a little. A condition Victoria cannot refuse.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: This is the price you must pay for trampling across our land.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: Ah!

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: There's... There's just... so much blood...

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: Degenbrecher!

steps.name: Sharp
steps.text: She needs emergency treatment. You got any more bandages here?

steps.name: Ratatos
steps.text: I... I'll go find some!

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: Degenbrecher... How did you get so hurt?

steps.name: Sharp
steps.text: She held off seventeen Trilby Ashers by herself. She's something, alright.

steps.name: Sharp
steps.text: The enemy's retreated for now, so my team will take over guarding this place from her.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: But there's still so many Victorian soldiers out there... What will you...?

steps.name: Sharp
steps.text: I'll keep going until my mission is complete.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: More people are going to get hurt...

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: Is something going on outside again?

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: Let me reconfirm: orders are to... carry out a frontal assault on the Vine-Bead Court?

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: Assault the Vine-Bead Court and rescue the abducted Victorian citizen.

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: ...And capture Ratatos, who might be carrying key military secrets of Kjerag.

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: ...Acknowledged.

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: All hands, load live ammunition.

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: We storm the Court.

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Pious Cleric
steps.text: Before you is holy ground. None may enter as they please.

steps.name: Pious Cleric
steps.text: Please leave.

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: If you don't wish to be harmed, then let us through. That is an order.

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: Are you... refusing?

steps.name: Pious Cleric
steps.text: You have obeyed your orders in coming here. So too, do we obey Kjeragandr's commands as we do the same.

steps.name: Pious Cleric
steps.text: Let us follow our hearts, and do what we must do.

a.text: Enya has changed into her most solemn of clothes, treading once more onto the road that tested the Saintesses.
She thinks of the countless Saintesses of a millennium ago who walked this rocky path. Her every step echoes with theirs across the ages.
What wishes did they carry with them when they met with the Kjeragandr of their hearts? Did any of them question the existence of their god, and did any of them receive Her favor?
As for her... How did she climb this mountain the first time around?
It was such a long time ago. The emotions she felt have become hazy. Her memories of the time have begun to deform.
Enya never thought this road could be so smooth, so friendly.
As if she were taking a relaxing walk home, or preparing to go meet a dear friend whom she had not seen in a long while.
The gray-yellow sky is covered in thick clouds, streaked with faint lightning. The chill winds have picked up.
Enya kneels, shuts her eyes, and begins to pray.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: If... you can still hear my voice.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: If you are still the merciful Kjeragandr who loves all men who live here...

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: My beloved Kjeragandr, this is the last time... I ask that you hear my prayer.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I have asked countless times what made Kjerag Kjerag, what made us the way we are.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Your existence might not be the answer to this question, but it is still a... small miracle, one to rejoice in.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I want to believe that the things you left upon this land are blessings, not shackles.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: Throughout the centuries, you have accompanied our civilization as it grew, as a loving and wise teacher.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: And centuries from now, the people of this land will have the power to move mountains and touch the sky, yet they shall still praise your name.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: We will remember your kindness. We will thank you for your companionship. We will leave the cradle of your protection.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: I ask that you allow me to be your vicar, so that I may protect Kjerag one last time.

steps.name: Enya
steps.text: This is my... final prayer...
Light shines from her palm. A gentle force calms the raging wind, stilling even the flow of time itself across this ancient land.
The Catastrophe clouds begin to scatter. The dread disaster about to strike the land has been subdued by some awesome might.
The clouds part, showering the devout woman in a kindly radiance.
The wind stops.

steps.name: Rhine Lab Researcher
steps.text: A Catastrophe alert?!

steps.name: Rhine Lab Researcher
steps.text: That's some good timing. We only just installed this warning device, and it's already coming in handy!

steps.name: Rhine Lab Researcher
steps.text: We need to inform the government to evacuate people right away... Oh no, the danger level—

steps.name: Kjerag Researcher
steps.text: The alert... stopped all of a sudden?

steps.name: Kjerag Researcher
steps.text: But how...? This steep drop in Originium energy fluctuations... Are the monitors broken, or...?

steps.name: Kjerag Researcher
steps.text: By Kjeragandr...
The old man hobbles along the rugged trail, walking towards the depths of the mountains. It is where he has consigned himself to.
He stops by the side of a cliff.
Why do you wish to jump?

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: All my life... I have lived a lie.

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: I should have been Her servant... but I deceived Her. Deceived myself.

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: It was my arrogance, my impiety, that led me down this undignified and evil road.

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: I cannot... forgive myself. All I can do is end this sinful life.

steps.name: Passing Girl
steps.text: But if this is how you go, all the snows can do is bury your body. They can't cover up your mistakes.

steps.name: Passing Girl
steps.text: No confession comes too late. You need only repent in your heart, and you will be reborn.

steps.name: Passing Girl
steps.text: You know, I can't quite recall... Kjeragandr, is that what She said?

steps.name: Passing Girl
steps.text: As Kjerag's most knowledgeable elder, there is still much you can do, right?

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: You...
The sky suddenly clears, the fierce sunlight dazzling the old man's eyes.
He sees the rays of light tear through the clouds. His chest, too, seems to burn.

steps.name: Adso
steps.text: Is this... a miracle...?

steps.name: Passing Girl
steps.text: Just this once, Enya... From now on, everything really is in your hands.

steps.name: Passing Girl
steps.text: Sorry. When the time is right, I'll come see you.

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: This is your final warning. This operation is not targeted at Kjerag's civilians. Please leave immediately!

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: If you refuse to cooperate, we cannot guarantee your safety.
The officer raises his blade high as he gives the civilians a stern warning, but none of them budge.
Soon, more and more people begin to gather.
Clerics, craftsmen, herdsmen, merchants... They stand across from the soldiers by their own accord, forming a silent wall.
One person squeezes out from the crowd. She raises her hands, walking between the two groups.
Several operators dressed in Rhodes Island uniforms follow behind her.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: I'm... the 'hostage' you said you were going to rescue.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: The people of Kjerag never abducted me. In fact, it was Victorian agents who trapped me in there, trying to destroy the evidence I have of Victorian operations in Kjerag. They even harmed the people trying to protect me.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: All the evidence, that evidence you want so badly, is hidden somewhere you cannot touch. If you make any further moves, it will be immediately released to the public.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: If you still want to silence me, then do as you will.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: But these crimes you have committed on sovereign Kjerag land, under the banner of 'nobility'... You will never be able to cover them up.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: We're not any sort of superior civilization. We're just better at cheating and swindling.

steps.name: Alberta
steps.text: Just stop it already... This farce.

steps.name: Victorian Commander
steps.text: You...
The gloomy sky suddenly clears. As one, everyone lifts their heads.
The clouds covering the heavens disperse, replaced by a rainbow spanning the horizon.
And so, all cruelty and fear are wiped from the hearts of men.
The sunlight dazzles the eyes, as if it were advice, or perhaps deterrent.
The soldiers cannot help but lay down their arms.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Time is short.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I am afraid that things will not turn for the better, if you delay.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What is Your Grace's decision?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I am suddenly reminded of something you once said...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I could never imagine what sort of power a united nation might possess... Is today the day I get to experience it for myself?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What you see is but one minute aspect of it. If you ever have the chance to deepen your understanding of her, I believe you will be very much pleasantly surprised.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: In truth, this is a topic I only fully understood long after I left Victoria. Perhaps it can also answer the question you posed me.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Why once-great empires become feeble, and how poor lands can stand tall.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: A nation's government, its institutions... Whether its leader is the Lord of Lions or Parliament, whether Saintess or the Clans.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: These are important things to consider, yes... but the crux shall forever be the people.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: Just as a great navigator cannot hope to lead a hole-pocked flotilla forward, no leader can change the fate of a nation using solely their own strength.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: You say that, yet your words do not agree with your actions.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Were you not prepared to change the destiny of all Kjerag with your own two hands?

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I believe in the people who live upon this land. People of faith.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: I know you have devised all sorts of means to confirm if the mysterious power of the famed Kjeragandr truly does protect Kjerag.

steps.name: Enciodes
steps.text: What you see, what blocks your way, is indeed Kjeragandr's might.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Haha... You are the same as you ever were.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Still so full of mettle, so eager to display yourself... Impressive.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: This little gamble of yours has managed to get the better of me... But this time, I will not let you off easy the way I do with mediocre men.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: And so—

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: ...Huh?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: What... is that?
The people on deck look to the distance.
They see the thick clouds layered across the sky be torn open by some divine power. They see the ancient Mount Karlan, bathed in radiance.
It is a beautiful sight. Enough to stir the hearts of people, and inspire reverence.
Is it Her wroth, or Her mercy?
The word 'holy' might never have come to the minds of the irreligious, but at this moment, the same thought blooms in the hearts of all.
This is a pure land, one that must not be violated.

steps.name: Anxious Soldier
steps.text: Your Grace... Our intelligence indicates that this 'Kjeragandr' has already vanished from Kjerag.

steps.name: Anxious Soldier
steps.text: But we cannot confirm what is causing this phenomenon in the sky.

steps.name: Anxious Soldier
steps.text: What should we do, Your Grace?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: I had wanted to see this gamble through...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: But unfortunately, they have added one last weight to the balance, and we cannot stop the scales of victory from pointing their way.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: What more can we even do?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Sound the retreat.
